claim: Engram retrieval bandwidth is not the bottleneck for offload: at 70,000 tokens/s with two Engram layers the memory pool needs only about 0.7 GB/s, easily served by PCIe Gen5 (64 GB/s) or 100GbE (12.5 GB/s).
stance_target: Whether PCIe bandwidth constrains Engram table offload
scope_conditions: Qwen3-32B emulation in SGLang, 4x H200 cluster, 2 Engram layers at k=2 and 15, 5 KB/token/layer
quoted_support: At a throughput of 70k tokens/s, the total required read bandwidth is B_pool = T x S_layer x N_eng ~ 0.7 GB/s. It is easily accommodated by PCIe Gen5 (64 GB/s) or 100GbE network (12.5 GB/s). Thus, bandwidth is not the primary bottleneck for Engram offloading.

claim: Engram retrieval latency is the real constraint: with t_step ~3.6 ms across 64 layers, per-layer compute is ~56 us, so an Engram module at layer 2 has only a ~56 us prefetch window to hide the memory access.
stance_target: That lookup latency, not bandwidth, governs whether offloaded Engram tables stall the GPU
scope_conditions: Qwen3-32B on 4x H200, batch 256, 512-token in/out, 64 layers
quoted_support: Given t_step ~3.6ms across 64 layers, the average computation time per layer (t_exec) is approximately 56 us. For an Engram module at Layer 2, the prefetch window in the system is restricted to about 56 us. This is a stringent requirement for pooled memory systems.

claim: Engram fetches only about 5 KB of data per token per layer - 16 discrete embeddings of 320 bytes each for N-gram=2 with 8 hash heads - so per-token transfer volume is tiny relative to table size.
stance_target: Whether Engram offload traffic scales with table size or with activated slots
quoted_support: In current configurations, the model fetches only 5 KB of data per token per layer. This payload consists of 16 discrete, small-scale embeddings (based on N-gram = 2 and 8 hash heads) among massive Engram table.

claim: RDMA-based memory pooling incurs latency orders of magnitude above local DRAM for Engram's fine-grained sparse retrieval, whereas CXL pooling tracks local DRAM closely.
stance_target: Which pooling fabric is viable for Engram table offload
scope_conditions: Two-server testbed, Mooncake Store for RDMA, XConn XC50256 CXL switch with 256 GB Samsung CXL card, batch sizes 1 to 1024
quoted_support: The profiling results indicate that RDMA incurs a latency penalty orders of magnitude higher than that of local DRAM. In contrast, CXL-based memory pooling delivers latencies that closely approximate local DRAM, aligning well with the latency timing requirements of Engram prefetching.

claim: CXL-based Engram pooling achieves near-DRAM end-to-end throughput in SGLang, with only a small gap between DRAM-backed and CXL-backed Engram.
stance_target: Whether offloading Engram tables to pooled memory costs inference throughput
scope_conditions: Single L20 GPU, DP=1, batch 256, 512-token input/output, Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B emulating Engram

claim: The Engram-27B table configuration is vocab_size 2,262,400 with embedding dimension 1,280, and Engram-40B uses vocab_size 7,239,680 with the same 1,280 dimension.
stance_target: The concrete table dimensions needed for memory-footprint arithmetic
scope_conditions: Engram-27B and Engram-40B configurations as profiled
quoted_support: We evaluate the CXL read latency for Engram embeddings under Engram-27B (vocab_size = 2,262,400; emb_dim = 1,280) and Engram-40B (vocab_size = 7,239,680; emb_dim = 1,280) configurations.

claim: Engram memory is read-only and immutable during inference, which is why the CXL pool avoids maintaining cross-node cache coherence.
stance_target: Whether Engram offload requires coherence machinery
quoted_support: Since the Engram embeddings are read-only, the system avoid the overhead of maintaining cache coherence across nodes.

claim: The CXL prototype uses a single 256 GB CXL memory card holding the entire Engram table, shared across servers through a CXL switch with 512 GB/s aggregate bandwidth and support for up to 8 servers on a 4 TB pool.
stance_target: The hardware scale required to pool Engram tables
scope_conditions: XConn XC50256 CXL switch, 256 PCIe 5.0 lanes, Samsung memory card with Montage M88MX5851 controller
quoted_support: The CXL switch chip can provide 512 GB/s of total bandwidth between memory devices and compute servers, which connects up to 8 servers to a 4 TB memory pool.

claim: This study is inference-only: it emulates Engram inside SGLang using Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B because open-source Engram weights and models do not exist, and it does not address training-time gradient or optimizer traffic.
stance_target: Whether CXL pooling evidence applies to training
quoted_support: Due to the lack of open-source Engram weights and models, we utilizes Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B to emulate the performance. To reflect the overhead, Engram computations are executed during the forward pass and the retrieved embeddings are not added to the hidden states to preserve model stability.
